elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The carve-out is limited to a “financially responsible affiliate,” so it does not permit assignment to every affiliate.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The Client may assign without approval “to a successor in a merger.”

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The Client may assign without approval “to a successor in an…acquisition.”

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all of its assets.
elements.evidence: The Client may assign without approval “to a successor in a…sale of substantially all of its assets.”

elements.element: Vendor may not make any assignment without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The mutual financially responsible affiliate exception permits Vendor to assign to such an affiliate without Customer approval.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For assignments requiring approval, the clause states that approval “shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.”

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no competitor prohibition and could permit assignment to a competitor, including through the affiliate exception or with consent.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right arising from Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants no termination right based on Client's change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor.
elements.evidence: The Client-specific carve-out permits assignment without approval to a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization, or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no written-notice obligation for a Client successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may assign without consent to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor carve-out applies only “in the case of Client”; Vendor has no general consent-free successor right.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no written-notice obligation for a Vendor successor assignment.

elements.element: Every Customer assignment other than a successor assignment requires Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: A Client assignment to a financially responsible affiliate requires no approval even if the affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Customer assignment for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard applies mutually to approval required under the clause.

elements.element: Every Vendor assignment other than a successor assignment requires Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Vendor may assign to a financially responsible affiliate without Customer approval, even where the affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard applies to Customer's approval of Vendor assignments requiring consent.

result.reason: The redline gives Client the requested successor carve-outs and adds a mutual reasonableness standard, but it does not reach either complete position. It retains a consent-free Vendor affiliate assignment right, lacks the absolute competitor prohibition, gives no general successor right to Vendor, and requires no written notice of successor assignments. It also adds reorganization and a prohibition on unreasonable delay, which are related but beyond the stated positions. The language remains coherent and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms.
